name.text: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — solving sin^-1(x) = theta for x

questiontext.text:
Suppose \( \sin^{-1}(x) = {@thetadeg@}^\circ \), where \({@thetadeg@}^\circ\) lies within the principal range of \(\sin^{-1}\).

Find the exact value of \(x\).

\(x = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
\(\sin^{-1}(x)={@thetadeg@}^\circ\) means exactly the same thing as \(x=\sin({@thetadeg@}^\circ)\) — to undo the \(\sin^{-1}\), apply \(\sin\) to both sides.

\[ x = \sin({@thetadeg@}^\circ) = {@ta@}. \]

A common slip is to leave \(x\) as the angle itself (\({@thetadeg@}\)) instead of evaluating \(\sin\) of that angle.
